authorization: etymologise remaining Indo-Aryan surveys. do not rebuild. work autonomously and do what you can, you have 8 hours, i will review once your time is done.

proposals.evidence: In the third section Turner separates *valkhala and *vōlkala, placing Nepali bokro and Hindi boklā after the o-vowel branch. These northern survey bokr-/bokl- bark forms match that specific *vōlkala formation and ordinary final vowel variation. Aspirated or retroflex-extended responses are left unresolved rather than combined with the a-vowel valkala branch.

proposals.evidence: Turner’s onomatopoeic *kutta family includes Punjabi/Lahnda kuttā, West Pahari kuttā, Nepali kuti, Oriya kutā, Hindi kuttā and Gujarati kuttɔ. These whole survey dog forms fit that regional family, retaining the source’s dental/retroflex and occasional aspirated spellings as expressive variation rather than a claimed regular sound law. r-bearing and doubly aspirated responses are excluded.

proposals.evidence: The second *sūṅkara subsection explicitly lists Nepali sũgar/sũgur, Kumaoni sũgar and Jaunsari sũgar, with Koci suṅgur in the addendum. The survey sugar/sugur forms retain g like that regional branch, unlike the ordinary sūkara > suar series; absent nasal marking and source aspiration notation remain visible.
